scope: Deploys the two fixed-address infrastructure contracts that the pinned x402-rs facilitator image (ghcr.io/x402-rs/x402-facilitator@sha256:89ab5c031f48bdb61837a0e0ebd296d9f5d3d34eb49183f5472774ab1b119b0d, x402-rs rev 0b14f39afb604a7df25b3496ba34122bdca45a7f) hardcodes in its `assert_contracts_exists` startup check for every configured eip155 chain. This does not enable an upto/Permit2 payment route, credit top-up, or production use; it only satisfies the facilitator's unconditional startup invariant so eip155:91342 can be configured at all. Deployed alongside the already-present canonical Permit2 (0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3, OP Stack preinstall) and the Arachnid CREATE2 deployer (0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C, OP Stack preinstall).

create2Deployer.provenance: Arachnid deterministic deployment proxy, OP Stack preinstall

permit2.provenance: Canonical Uniswap Permit2 address, OP Stack preinstall
permit2.note: Already present on GIWA Sepolia prior to this deployment; not re-deployed here. See contracts/deployments/giwa-sepolia-x402-upto-v1.json for its observed runtime code hash.

exactPermit2Proxy.provenanceNote: The pinned initCodeHash is only reproducible from the upstream-frozen script/data/exact-proxy-initcode.hex artifact, not from a fresh forge build (original x402-foundation build embedded non-deterministic CBOR metadata). runtimeCodeHash was independently cross-verified by CREATE2-deploying the pinned initCodeHash through the real Arachnid deployer on a disposable local anvil instance before this real GIWA Sepolia deployment; the anvil gas usage (709183) matched the real deployment exactly.

erc6492Validator.create2SaltNote: Vanity-mined salt; the first 4 bytes decode as ASCII "x402", zero-padded to 32 bytes.

sourceProvenance.method: Sourcify v2 verified match (not a git-revision pin, since this contract has no known x402-foundation source repository attribution)

onChainCreationRecord.note: Confirms `to` is the Arachnid CREATE2 deployer; salt and 2402-byte init code were extracted directly from this transaction's calldata (32-byte salt prefix + init code, no constructor args).

sourceProvenance.distinctFromAmbireCanonicalDeployment: This is a separate CREATE2 deployment of the same open-source Ambire Validator6492 contract (identical source/interface), not Ambire's own canonical ERC-2470 singleton at 0x7dD271FA79Df3A5fEB99F73Bebfa4395b2e4f4bE. Different salt, different resulting address.
sourceProvenance.crossChainRuntimeObservation: The runtime code hash observed on GIWA Sepolia after this deployment (0x9b83857b...) matches both the local anvil pre-deployment dry-run and the address's runtime code as independently observed on Base mainnet, giving three-way cross-chain agreement.

erc6492Validator.note: Not registered in contracts/scripts/verify-source-locks.mjs's automated SOURCE_LOCK_PATHS gate: this contract's provenance format (Sourcify match + on-chain creation-tx record) does not fit the git-revision-pin pattern that script validates, and registering it there would falsely imply automated-CI-gate status for a fundamentally different kind of evidence.

verification.method: For each contract: (1) derived/obtained salt and init code from a verifiable upstream source (frozen vendor artifact for the Exact proxy; the real on-chain CREATE2 creation transaction for the validator), (2) reproduced the exact canonical address via `cast compute-address`, (3) pre-verified expected gas usage and runtime code hash by CREATE2-deploying through the real Arachnid deployer on a disposable local anvil instance, (4) deployed to GIWA Sepolia via `cast send` to the Arachnid deployer using the funded dev wallet, (5) confirmed receipt status 0x1 and re-read runtime code hash and (for the Exact proxy) the PERMIT2() getter through the validation RPC.
verification.ironRule: Only init code whose cast compute-address via the Arachnid deployer reproduces exactly the required hardcoded address (0xdAcD51A54883eb67D95FAEb2BBfdC4a9a6BD2a3B or 0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001) was deployed. No substitute or approximate bytecode was ever considered.
